title: Invariant ordinary exceptional counit and graded ordinary adjunction
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime $\ell\ne D.p$, normalized family R, model spaces X,Y, any ForgetModels $V_X,V_Y$, a separated quasi-compact locally finite-type $f_0:X.base\to Y.base$, a normalized coefficient system S and a compactification c of the geometric map, as in [def-sf-native-exceptional-forgetful-data]. Write $F\dashv G$ for S.ring.operation c .closed and J for native compact support. Let $E_Y$ be actual ordinary closure transport followed by the specified section-module presentation; VY.realization identifies $V_Y;\rho_Y$ with $U_Y;E_Y$. Use the fixed graded transport tau of [lem-sf-native-exceptional-hom-transport]. There exists $a:J;V_Y\cong V_X;F$ such that for every native L in W(Y) there exist native H in W(X), $e:V_XH\cong GV_YL$, and an ordinary native-adic derived arrow $t:U_YJH\to U_YL$. Writing r for VY.realization, one has $E_Y(t)=r_{JH}^{-1};\rho_Y(a_H;F(e);\epsilon_{V_YL});r_L$. The arrow t followed by the canonical inverse zero-shift identification belongs to the actual degree-zero invariant subgroup of [def-sf-cyclic-derived-hom-data]. For every native K and every integer r, the ordinary map $v\mapsto\tau_r(v);t[r]$ from degree-r Hom(K,H) to degree-r Hom(JK,L) is bijective. No native lift of t, boundary compatibility, or equivalence on invariants or coinvariants is asserted.

proof.text: The scalar-normalized Frobenius mate gives an invertible action on the ordinary exceptional image of VY(L). Apply cyclic derived action realization. Its interval preservation and constructibility give native H and action-compatible e. Under the fixed comparisons the ordinary counit is t and satisfies the transported-arrow equation. The mate-counit identity proves its Frobenius invariance; zero-shift coherence gives the asserted kernel membership.

proof.text: In each integer degree compose the shifted ordinary adjunction bijection with e[r] and the specified shift comparisons. Counit naturality and the shift-counit identity identify its inverse formula with tau_r(v) followed by t[r], proving ordinary Hom bijectivity. No boundary or native morphism lift enters this ordinary calculation.

theorem native_exceptional_ordinary_counit (R : Family l D)
    (X Y : Space D) (VX : ForgetModel D l R X) (VY : ForgetModel D l R Y)
    (f₀ : X.base ⟶ Y.base)
    [IsSeparated f₀.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left] [QuasiCompact f₀.left]
    (S : CoefficientSystem D l f₀) (c : Compactification (geometricMap D f₀)) :
    ∃ a : nativeShriek D l f₀ ⋙ VY.functor ≅
        VX.functor ⋙ (S.ring.operation c .closed).F,
      ∀ L : W D l Y, ∃ (H : W D l X)
        (e : VX.functor.obj H ≅ (S.ring.operation c .closed).G.obj (VY.functor.obj L))
        (t : WeilComplex.forget.obj ((nativeShriek D l f₀).obj H) ⟶
          WeilComplex.forget.obj L),
        (counitOrdinaryTransport D l R Y).map t =
          VY.realization.inv.app ((nativeShriek D l f₀).obj H) ≫
            (rho D l R Y).map (a.hom.app H ≫ (S.ring.operation c .closed).F.map e.hom ≫
              (S.ring.operation c .closed).adjunction.counit.app (VY.functor.obj L)) ≫
            VY.realization.hom.app L ∧
        (t ≫ (shiftFunctorZero _ ℤ).inv.app (WeilComplex.forget.obj L)) ∈
          CyclicDerivedHomInvariants (WeilSheaf.frobeniusPullback D.k₀ l Y.base.left)
            ((nativeShriek D l f₀).obj H).obj L.obj ∧
        ∀ (K : W D l X) (r : ℤ), Function.Bijective
          (fun v : CyclicDerivedHom (WeilSheaf.frobeniusPullback D.k₀ l X.base.left)
            K.obj H.obj r ↦ counitHomTransport D l f₀ K H r v ≫ t⟦r⟧')
